name: gupnp-av
desc: Library to help implement UPnP A/V profiles
why: A GNOME library for UPnP A/V profiles, a door into the media discovery protocol running on home routers and TVs.

brief.what_it_is: GUPnP A/V is a small utility library, according to its GitLab project page, that aims to ease the handling and implementation of UPnP A/V profiles. UPnP A/V is the family of UPnP media profiles used by networked audio and video devices. The library is aimed at developers writing software that speaks those profiles. The GitLab page does not say what inputs or outputs the API takes, and I could not retrieve the README body or API docs to confirm them. The scout note's description of it as a door into the media discovery protocol on home routers and TVs is the scout's framing, not something I saw in the project text.
brief.why_it_exists: The project page says it exists to ease the handling and implementation of UPnP A/V profiles. The wiki homepage gives no further framing.
brief.install_notes: Nothing found. The homepage and GitLab page give no build, dependency, or install instructions. The README body did not load, so any build steps (such as meson or autotools) are unverified.
brief.standout: It is a GNOME-hosted library for a protocol family that most people only meet indirectly, through TVs, media servers, and routers. Beyond that, I could not verify anything distinctive from the text I could read.
brief.status: Probably maintained, but unconfirmed. The GitLab project page shows a creation date of May 23, 2018, but I saw no last-release or last-commit date. The old wiki homepage is marked as retired, and it points to handbook.gnome.org and gitlab.gnome.org for current information, so the project has moved to GitLab.
brief.caveats: The wiki homepage is a retirement notice with no project content, so I relied on the GitLab project page for the description. The README body did not load, and I found no commands, install steps, platform notes, or API examples. The GitLab page lists the license as GNU LGPLv2.1. The brew formula has no executables, which fits a library rather than a command-line tool.
quotes: GUPnP A/V is a small utility library that aims to ease the handling and implementation of UPnP A/V profiles.
This site has been retired. For up to date information, see handbook.gnome.org or gitlab.gnome.org.
